title: Take coupon codes at checkout
context:
Customers ask support for discounts by email today, and support refunds the difference by hand. The checkout total already takes a discount (it is zero everywhere), so a coupon only has to supply that number.

Out of frame: an admin screen for making coupons, and gift cards. This plan seeds coupons from a migration.

decisions.decision: Check the code on the server, not in the form
decisions.why: a code checked only in the browser can be replayed with any discount the client sends

adr.consequences: every coupon costs one lookup per checkout; the form shows the discount only after the server answers
alternatives: validate in the form and trust the posted discount
sign the discount into the cart

decisions.decision: Keep coupons in their own table
decisions.why: orders keep their shape, and a coupon can be turned off without touching any order
stacking rules were not asked for, and one code keeps the total easy to explain on the receipt

contracts.reach: the web checkout form is the only caller (src/checkout/route.js); the field is optional, so old carts still check out
contracts.decisionRef: Check the code on the server, not in the form

contracts.reach: read by the coupon lookup only; nothing else queries it
contracts.decisionRef: Keep coupons in their own table

verifiedFacts.claim: the checkout total already takes a discount
checkout is the only caller of total()
orders store only the final total

risks.risk: whether codes are case-sensitive was never decided
an expired coupon could stay in a browser tab and fail at the last step
the support team may already hand out codes that clash with new ones
risks.note: ask support for last month's codes and diff them against the seed

risks.risk: percent-off rounding may differ from what support refunds by hand today

diagrams.question: What happens when a customer enters a code?
diagrams.simple:
flowchart LR
  A[Customer types a code] --> B[Shop checks it]
  B --> C[Discount shown]
  C --> D[Pays the lower total]
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  F[checkout form] -->|POST /checkout + coupon| R[route.js]
  R --> L[coupons/lookup.js]
  L --> T[(coupons)]
  L -->|percent_off| R
  R --> X[total.js discount]
  X --> F

diagrams.question: Which states can a coupon be in?
diagrams.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> active
  active --> expired: expires_at passes
  active --> disabled: turned off
  expired --> [*]
  disabled --> active: turned on

deliverables.title: Coupon lookup
deliverables.body: lookup(code) returns the percent off for a live coupon, or null for an unknown or expired one.

checks.name: coupon_applied counter climbs in dev
checks.expect: above zero after a test checkout

deliverables.title: Apply the coupon at checkout
deliverables.body: POST /checkout takes an optional coupon, looks it up, and passes the discount to total(). An expired code gets a 422 with a message the form can show.

deliverables.title: Coupons table
deliverables.body: A migration that creates the coupons table and seeds WELCOME10.
deliverables.waiver: the lookup tests in increment 1 read the seeded rows; a migration has nothing of its own to prove

quiz.prompt: A customer edits the page to send 90% off along with a real code. What do they pay?
quiz.why: the server looks the code up and ignores any discount the client sends
quiz.decisionRef: Check the code on the server, not in the form

quiz.prompt: Support turns a coupon off. What changes for orders already placed?
quiz.why: coupons live in their own table and orders store only the final total
quiz.decisionRef: Keep coupons in their own table

quiz.prompt: A customer has two codes. What can they do?
quiz.why: one coupon per order; stacking is a non-goal

quiz.prompt: A customer types welcome10 for the code WELCOME10. What happens?
quiz.why: promoted risk, decided here: codes match without regard to case
quiz.riskRef: whether codes are case-sensitive was never decided
quiz.decisionRef: Check the code on the server, not in the form
